summary.intent: Plan, execute, and ship GSD Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability/correctness) for CipherBox, including todo housekeeping and a dependency check against Phase 73, while unblocking a concurrent CI outage (web-e2e, desktop-e2e, sdk-e2e failures) that was discovered mid-flow.
summary.outcome: Phase 72 was fully planned (research + pattern-mapping + 10-plan wave execution with TDD), all 6 success criteria implemented and verified, a full test-file TypeScript drift cleanup + CI typecheck gate were added, a real DoS-class cycle-guard bug was found and fixed, three CI regressions (web-e2e floor store, FUSE seq equivocation, sdk-e2e Test 21 flake) were fixed and merged via PR #601/#600, and PR #602 for Phase 72 was opened; a HIGH-severity security finding (moveItem missing baseWriteChildren, allowing write-chain resurrection) was caught by a post-execution security review and a fix was in progress when the transcript ends.

repo: vitest does not load .env — the sdk-e2e harness reads process.env.SDK_E2E_SECRET with a hardcoded fallback secret, so forgetting to export it silently sends the wrong secret and yields a 401, not an obvious config error.

ci-e2e.yml (Web + Desktop E2E) triggers only on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on pull_request — must dispatch manually via `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (not `-f ref=`, which 422s on older workflow defs) to validate a branch pre-merge.

Local Playwright runs are systematically tighter than CI: `ciFloor()` only raises wait timeouts to 60s under CI, so IPNS-gated mutation waits (delete/restore/mkdir/batch-ops) that pass in CI reliably flake locally under the 15-30s local timeouts.

playwright.config.ts webServer.reuseExistingServer is keyed off `!process.env.CI`, so setting CI=1 locally to get the CI timeout floor also breaks server reuse against an already-running stack — requires a temporary config patch to reconcile.

@cipherbox/* packages have no path aliases or TS project references — cross-package types resolve through the workspace symlink to each package's built `dist`, so a CI typecheck gate must run build-then-typecheck in dependency order, not typecheck-before-build.

Root `pnpm typecheck` previously only ran each package's `tsconfig.build.json` (tests excluded) — test files were never typechecked in CI, allowing ~113 errors (vitest v2→v3 Mock generics drift + Phase-62 retired-type imports) to accumulate silently in test files.

GSD executor commits use non-conventional subjects (`feat 51-03:`, `refactor sdk:`) that fail the pr-release-preview/commitlint gate; since `git rebase -i` is unavailable, reword via `git filter-branch --msg-filter` and verify the tree is byte-identical after.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL) — patch the PR body via `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file` instead.

Phase 71 (#599) shipped without retiring 8 of its own source todos from pending/ to completed/, and left behind 3 pieces of test/fixture drift (stale .mts DTO field names, a non-idempotent sdk-e2e assertion, and a real FUSE seq=1 bug) — ship checklists should verify source-todo retirement and CI health as part of done-ness.

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on first-publish gated only by 'inode cid empty', so a dropped/stale UploadComplete re-triggered first-publish with a new CID at seq=1, colliding with Phase 71's anti-equivocation gate. Fixed by resolving IPNS first and routing Found into the existing CAS-retry path instead of skip/first-publish.

publish_with_cas_retry gained an optional preresolved_seq param (Greptile P2 fix) so the file-publish caller's guard-resolve isn't redundantly repeated; conflict-retry path still always re-resolves since a pre-resolved value is stale after a conflict.

collectDescendantIpnsNames had no cycle guard (unlike sibling dfsFindFolder's visited Set), allowing unbounded recursion / hang on a cyclic or malicious folder graph — a real DoS-class bug surfaced only when re-enabling a previously stub-skipped test.

Base-aware CAS-merge: when params.baseWriteChildren is undefined, the merge falls back to a naive union where remote entries always win — this resurrects a WriteChildRef a caller deliberately dropped if a racing writer's stale snapshot still carries it.

moveItem's source-folder publish drops the moved child's WriteChildRef (same operation as deleteItem) but never threads baseWriteChildren into updateFolderMetadataAndPublish, unlike deleteItem/restoreFromBin which were fixed in this phase — leaving a live write-chain resurrection gap on an operation named in the phase's own goal (delete/move/restore/replace).

workflow: For a phase whose plans are ~90% serialized on one shared file (client.ts), prefer sequential execution on the main tree over per-plan worktree isolation — worktrees add setup cost and risk missing node_modules in a pnpm monorepo, with no real parallelism benefit when files aren't disjoint.

When a background local test run cascades due to an early flaky/slow step, don't keep re-running the same regime — switch to running under the CI-equivalent timeout/env regime (e.g. CI=1) to get a representative pass/fail instead of chasing a different transient failure each run.

Ship-phase operating rule (fix in-scope+low-risk now, defer pre-existing/out-of-scope/risky as a todo) worked well to keep a long autonomous run moving without stalling on every review finding, but the security-reviewer subagent still caught a real HIGH-severity gap (moveItem) that unit/e2e tests and the plan-checker had missed — an independent adversarial review pass after execution is valuable even when all gates are green.

When dispatching multiple background jobs/agents that touch the same file (e.g. a fix agent and a manual edit both touching client.ts), sequence them explicitly rather than running concurrently to avoid races — confirmed by deliberately waiting on 72-04 before starting 72-05, and by staging security-review fixes only after the moveItem fix agent's client.ts edits landed.

friction: `gh workflow run -f ref=` returned HTTP 422 'Unexpected inputs' because the workflow definition on main predates the `ref` input — required discovering the `--ref <branch>` alternative.
Initially checked the wrong todo directory (`resolved/` instead of `completed/`), corrected by the user mid-turn.

GSD hook JSON (plan:pre fragments) contained raw/multiline control characters that broke standard JSON parsing, requiring a custom lenient parser script to extract research/pattern-mapper/tdd fragments.

Local web-e2e verification devolved into a multi-hour whack-a-mole: fixing one flaky test (4.10) just exposed the next one downstream (4.11, then 2.1) under ambient load, because local timeouts are tighter than CI's ciFloor-raised ones — eventually required temporarily patching playwright.config.ts's reuseExistingServer to run under a true CI=1 regime.

Stale running API process on :3000 held an outdated TEST_LOGIN_SECRET even after restart-from-source appeared to succeed, and separately vitest's non-loading of .env caused SDK_E2E_SECRET to silently fall back to a placeholder — two separate causes of the same-looking 401, requiring careful hash-comparison diagnosis rather than assuming the first fix was sufficient.
A `git cat-file` check gave inconsistent signal about whether todo moves had landed in HEAD, temporarily causing confusion until a more decisive tree-content check resolved it.

Commit commands intermittently 'timed out'/reported failure due to a 1Password SSH-signing prompt hang while the commit had actually landed — required verifying via `git log` rather than retrying blindly (a known pattern already in project memory).

Non-conventional commit subjects produced by GSD executors (`feat 51-03:`, `refactor sdk:`) required a `git filter-branch --msg-filter` reword pass since interactive rebase isn't available in this environment.
open_items: moveItem missing baseWriteChildren (HIGH security finding) — fix + regression test dispatched to an agent but not yet confirmed landed/committed when the transcript ends.
share/shared-write.ts has no base-aware write-body merge at all (same resurrection-class exposure as moveItem) — explicitly deferred as a follow-up todo, not a Phase 72 regression.

registration.ts createSubfolder generates keys with no zeroization on a throw before return (CodeRabbit MAJOR finding) — deferred as pre-existing, low-severity, not corroborated by the security reviewer.
wrap.ts style suggestion to keep wrapIpnsKeyForTee in Uint8Array and move hex conversion to the boundary — deferred as a style-only todo.
bin/index.ts emptyBin/purgeExpired should drop lingering WriteChildRefs the same way permanentDeleteFromBin does, per CodeRabbit CLI finding — triage in progress, not yet fixed or deferred.
PR #602's PR-level CodeRabbit web review and Greptile review had not yet run/been processed when the transcript ends.
Dispatched web-e2e validation run (29109300364) against PR #602's branch was in progress, not yet confirmed green.
Phase 73 (including the folded-in 68.2-coderabbit-hardening-backlog web items) is queued to start once Phase 72 fully merges — not yet begun.
tee-republish.test.ts failures (tee_key_state table not seeded locally) remain an accepted local-only infra gap, not fixed, relying on CI's full TEE stack for coverage.
